title: Standards traceability: how the PoC fills CXP/CXF gaps

specifications.CXF: Credential Exchange Format, Proposed Standard with errata 2026-03-09 (cxf-v1.0-ps-errata-20260309), docs/specs/Credential_Exchange_Format.pdf

conventions.group: completion = a choice the PoC had to make for CXP/CXF to work at all, identical in both profiles; hardening = spec-minimal and hardened differ (or the gap is deliberately left open)
conventions.quote: verbatim text from the pinned PDF (null when the specification is silent; specSays then describes the silence)
conventions.section: null when a whole document is relied on or a guidance document has no numbered sections; verify=true when the exact section has not been confirmed and must be checked by the author
conventions.code: file:line where the behaviour is implemented (line of the declaration or check)

entries.title: HPKE suites and implementation
entries.quote: The value SHOULD be from the HPKE KEM Identifiers IANA table
entries.specSays: Suite identifiers come from the HPKE registries; CXP names no suite, and §5 (mandatory to implement) is empty (see GAP-02).
entries.choice: Importer offers DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256)/HKDF-SHA256/AES-256-GCM, then DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256)/HKDF-SHA256/AES-128-GCM, in base mode. The exporter supports KEM 0x0010/0x0020, KDF 0x0001 and AEAD 0x0001/0x0002/0xFFFF; ChaCha20-Poly1305 (0x0003) is not offered because it has no registered JOSE enc. Implementation: @hpke/core, validated against the RFC 9180 test vectors.
entries.summary: X25519 or P-256 KEM, HKDF-SHA256, AES-GCM; @hpke/core checked against RFC 9180 vectors
entries.designDecision: Preference order (MTI suite first, P-256 second) is a PoC choice: P-256 is offered for interoperability with WebCrypto-only stacks.

entries.title: JWK format of the importer key and of enc
entries.quote: It is a JSON Web Key representing that provider's key necessary for the other provider's generation of the AEAD key.
entries.specSays: The key is a JWK; the key type and parameters per KEM are not specified.
entries.choice: The HPKE serialised public key (also the format of enc) is carried as an OKP JWK {kty OKP, crv X25519, x} for X25519 and an EC JWK {kty EC, crv P-256, x, y} for P-256 (from the uncompressed point). On input the JWK must match the KEM, coordinates must be canonical base64url of the exact length.
entries.summary: OKP JWK for X25519, EC JWK for P-256; strict decoding

standards.role: EC public key parameters x, y

entries.title: JWE serialisation and header fields
entries.quote: All files are stored as JSON Web Encryption files.
entries.specSays: Files are JWE; serialisation, alg, enc and header members are not specified (the HPKE-to-JWE mapping is GAP-07).
entries.choice: Compact serialisation; protected header {alg: dir, enc: A128GCM | A256GCM} only (hardened adds cxp-path and cxp-req, GAP-09); no zip header. Decryption accepts only alg dir and the expected enc.
entries.summary: Compact JWE, alg dir, enc A128GCM/A256GCM, algorithm allow-list on decrypt

standards.role: zip header (deliberately not used, see GAP-27)

entries.title: base64url encoding of CXF b64url values
entries.quote: The b64url CDDL type is a [JSON] string which contains a [RFC4648] compliant URL-safe Base 64 encoded bytes.
entries.specSays: RFC 4648 URL-safe base64; padding and canonical form are not specified (acceptance rules are GAP-20).
entries.choice: Every b64url value the PoC writes is unpadded and canonical, as in the CXF Appendix A example.
entries.summary: Emit unpadded canonical base64url

entries.title: JSON encoding and unknown members
entries.quote: Any participant using this format MUST ignore unknown fields or enumeration values.
entries.specSays: CXF MUST support JSON encoding and MUST ignore unknown fields; whether ignored members are preserved is not stated.
entries.choice: Loose schemas: unknown members are ignored for processing but preserved, so a parsed document re-serialises to the same JSON value; round-trips are compared as JSON values, not bytes. Empty optional arrays are omitted on output (CXF §2.1.2 MUST).
entries.summary: Ignore-but-preserve unknown members; JSON-value round trip

standards.role: object member order is not significant
JSON-compatible CDDL prelude, as CXF §2.1 cites

entries.designDecision: Preserving unknown members keeps the CXF Appendix A round trip lossless.

entries.title: Integer range of uint .size 8
entries.quote: timestamp: uint .size 8,
entries.specSays: 64-bit unsigned integers in a JSON encoding; JSON number precision is not addressed.
entries.choice: Integers are accepted in 0..2^53-1, the range JSON numbers represent exactly in JavaScript.
entries.summary: uint64 fields limited to 0..2^53-1

standards.role: I-JSON: numbers beyond IEEE 754 double precision

entries.title: Request and response file format, naming and location
entries.quote: the Export Request SHALL be stored as a JSON-encoded document to be supplied to the Exporter by the Credential Owner.
entries.specSays: Both documents are JSON; file names, location and encoding details are not specified (permissions and removal are GAP-31).
entries.choice: UTF-8 JSON files named cxp-export-request.json and cxp-export-response-<UNIX seconds>.json in a caller-chosen directory (OS temporary directory, or out/indirect/ in the demo).
entries.summary: UTF-8 JSON files with fixed names in a caller-chosen directory

standards.role: UTF-8 for JSON text exchanged between systems

entries.designDecision: File names and location are not standardised anywhere; fixed descriptive names make the files easy to find in experiments.

entries.title: Direct-mode transport
entries.quote: In the case that a platform or Exporter provides an interface or transport over which the exchange ceremony can take place
entries.specSays: Direct mode uses a transport the platform or exporter provides; no transport is defined (its security is GAP-19).
entries.choice: JSON over HTTP: POST /cxp/export on 127.0.0.1, request body up to 256 KiB, response 200 with the Export Response or 400 with {error}. Requests whose mode is not direct are refused on this transport (GAP-23). Plain HTTP in spec-minimal, HTTPS in hardened (GAP-19).
entries.summary: HTTP POST /cxp/export on loopback, JSON bodies, 400 on error
entries.designDecision: The endpoint path and size limit are PoC choices; the transport is loopback only (README §9 rule 6).

entries.title: Passkey credential format of the software authenticator
entries.quote: The value MUST be PKCS#8 ASN.1 DER formatted byte string which is then Base64url encoded.
entries.specSays: The key is PKCS#8 DER; the algorithm is whatever the original authenticator used.
entries.choice: Both providers' software authenticators create ES256 (P-256) credentials with none attestation, encode COSE_Key and the attestation object as CTAP2-canonical CBOR, and sign authenticatorData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON). The importer stores only P-256 PKCS#8 keys (others are skipped and reported).
entries.summary: ES256 credentials, none attestation, canonical CBOR; importer accepts P-256 PKCS#8

standards.role: CTAP2 canonical CBOR encoding (map key order)

entries.designDecision: ES256 is the algorithm every WebAuthn RP accepts; a single algorithm keeps the authenticator small.

entries.title: Generation of CXF entity identifiers
entries.quote: An identifier for a given entity SHOULD be the same across different creations of a CXF document.
entries.specSays: IDs MUST be unique per Account and at most 64 bytes, SHOULD be stable and SHOULD NOT contain personal information; how to generate them is not specified.
entries.choice: Account and Item IDs are 128-bit values from the platform CSPRNG, created once per account / vault record and reused in every export. They are not derived from the credential ID, so an RP cannot recognise its own passkey among archive file names.
entries.summary: Random 128-bit IDs, fixed per record, not derived from credential IDs
entries.designDecision: No standard governs CXF ID generation; random, stable IDs satisfy the MUST and both SHOULDs.

entries.title: Non-passkey credentials
entries.quote: importers MAY attempt to store unknown item types in their own way as a best effort.
entries.specSays: Importers may store credential types they do not model.
entries.choice: Non-passkey credentials are parsed as opaque objects (preserved on round trip) but not imported; each is reported as skipped.
entries.summary: Other credential types kept opaque, not imported, reported
entries.designDecision: README §5 limits the PoC to passkeys; reporting skipped credentials keeps the behaviour observable.

entries.title: Loopback RP ID and origin for WebAuthn
entries.clause: Not CXP/CXF: W3C WebAuthn Level 3 RP ID validation
entries.specSays: CXP/CXF do not cover the RP; the demo RP must be a valid WebAuthn RP on loopback.
entries.choice: RP ID localhost, origin http://localhost:<port>, server bound to 127.0.0.1. The software client checks that the RP ID equals the origin host or a parent domain and that the origin is https or loopback; the public-suffix check is omitted (loopback only).
entries.summary: RP ID localhost; simplified client RP ID check

standards.role: client RP ID validation in create()

entries.title: Editorial defect in the direct-mode MUST
entries.quote: if indirect is requested, the Exporter MUST return the Export Response over the same transport or return an appropriate error.
entries.specSays: The direct-mode paragraph names indirect, which contradicts the indirect-mode MUST to write to the filesystem.
entries.choice: Read as direct: a direct request is answered over the same transport or with an error (HTTP 400).
entries.summary: Read 'indirect' as 'direct'
entries.designDecision: The only coherent reading of the paragraph.

entries.title: CXP version value
entries.quote: The version MUST correspond to a published level of the CXP standard.
entries.specSays: No level of CXP has been published, so no valid value exists.
entries.summary: version 0 (CDDL .default)
entries.designDecision: The CDDL default is the only value the specification itself supplies.

entries.title: CDDL contradicts prose
entries.quote: If this member is present but the list is empty, the Exporting Provider MUST send only the Account object without any Collection information.
entries.specSays: credentialTypes and knownExtensions are [+ ...] (non-empty) in CDDL, yet the prose defines empty lists; key is required in CDDL but 'only present' without a PSK in prose; unknown members are not addressed.
entries.choice: Follow the prose: empty lists accepted with their stated meaning, key optional in the schema (always sent in base/auth), unknown members ignored and kept.
entries.summary: Prose wins over CDDL
entries.designDecision: The prose states behaviour explicitly; the CDDL appears not to have been updated.

entries.title: What deflate compresses
entries.quote: Archiving through the use of the DEFLATE algorithm defined in [RFC1951].
entries.specSays: Whether DEFLATE applies to zip entries, to JWE plaintext or to the whole payload is not stated.
entries.choice: Zip entries use DEFLATE (compression method 8); JWE plaintexts are not compressed.
entries.summary: DEFLATE on zip entries; no JWE compression
entries.designDecision: Compressing before encryption can leak plaintext length information; compressing ciphertext is harmless.

entries.title: Meaning of 'correspond'
entries.quote: The value MUST correspond to an entry in hpke.
entries.specSays: The response key (enc) can never equal the request key, and 'correspond' is not defined.
entries.choice: Correspond = equal mode, kem, kdf and aead; the importer uses the private key of that request entry.
entries.summary: Equal mode/kem/kdf/aead
entries.designDecision: The four algorithm fields are the only members both objects can share.

entries.title: Response not bound to the request
entries.quote: The import request includes a challenge, the scope of the export request, and a declaration of the type of encryption scheme to be used.
entries.specSays: The overview describes a challenge and a signed challenge response, but neither exists in the CDDL.
entries.specMinimal: No challenge; HPKE info empty; a response is matched to the latest pending request.
entries.hardened: 32-byte random challenge in the request; SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical request is bound into HPKE info, so a response decrypts only for that exact request; the exporter refuses requests without a challenge.
entries.summary: Challenge + SHA-256(JCS(request)) bound into HPKE info

standards.role: info input to the key schedule

entries.title: No mandatory-to-implement suite
entries.quote: This section defines which algorithms and features of this specification are mandatory to implement.
entries.specSays: The section contains no algorithms.
entries.specMinimal: Any mutually listed suite is accepted, in the importer's order.
entries.hardened: Only DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) 0x0020 / HKDF-SHA256 0x0001 / AES-256-GCM 0x0002 is offered, selected and accepted.
entries.summary: MTI suite X25519 / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM only
entries.designDecision: Choosing one suite as mandatory is a design decision: no standard names a mandatory HPKE suite for CXP.

entries.title: Negotiated selection not integrity-protected
entries.quote: It is up to the Exporting Provider to select a matching set of parameters that both support.
entries.specSays: Nothing lets the importer check what the exporter chose against what it offered.
entries.specMinimal: Any selection present in the importer's lists is accepted.
entries.hardened: The importer requires the first HPKE entry and the first supported archive; with GAP-01 the offered lists are also bound into HPKE info.
entries.summary: Exporter must take the importer's first entries

standards.role: analogous practice: negotiation covered by the transcript hash

entries.designDecision: Requiring the first entry is stricter than TLS (which authenticates any choice); acceptable because the hardened importer offers one suite.

entries.title: Version downgrade
entries.quote: The Importing Provider MAY refuse this version downgrade.
entries.specSays: Refusal is optional.
entries.specMinimal: A lower response version is accepted.
entries.hardened: A response version below the requested version is rejected.
entries.summary: Reject version below the requested one

entries.title: Self-asserted importer/exporter identities
entries.quote: This member is the Relying Party Identifier of the Importing Provider.
entries.specSays: Both identities are plain claims with no authentication.
entries.specMinimal: Identities are display-only.
entries.hardened: The user compares 128-bit fingerprints shown by both providers: SHA-256 of the canonical request (direct channel) and the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the exporter's static key (importer side, with GAP-14).
entries.summary: 128-bit fingerprint comparison by the user

standards.role: JWK thumbprint of the exporter key
canonical request for the request fingerprint
rationale: short codes need a hash commitment (ZRTP SAS)

entries.designDecision: 128 bits (not a 6-digit SAS) because in indirect mode the request is seen before substitution, so a short code could be searched for offline.

entries.title: Unprotected request file
entries.quote: the Export Request SHALL be stored as a JSON-encoded document to be supplied to the Exporter by the Credential Owner.
entries.specSays: The file has no integrity protection on its way to the exporter.
entries.specMinimal: The file is loaded as-is.
entries.hardened: Before a file-channel export the exporter shows the request fingerprint; the user approves only if it matches the importer's display.
entries.summary: Request-file fingerprint confirmed before export

entries.title: HPKE-to-JWE mapping
entries.quote: where each file is separately encrypted using the key defined by the selected HPKE Parameters.
entries.specSays: How HPKE produces the JWE key, and where enc travels, are not specified.
entries.specMinimal: One payload key from the HPKE secret export (context "CXP payload key") is the CEK of every file; enc travels as a JWK in ExportResponse.hpke.key.
entries.hardened: A per-file key is exported with context "CXP file key " || path.
entries.summary: Per-file keys via HPKE secret export (label = path)

standards.role: IV uniqueness under one key (spec-minimal reuses a key with random IVs)

entries.designDecision: Exporter-context labels are PoC choices.

entries.title: Dangling 'anonymous identifier' for file names
entries.quote: The file names are replaced with the anonymous identifier in the export request.
entries.specSays: No such identifier exists in the §3.2 CDDL.
entries.specMinimal: Document names are CXF Item IDs.
entries.hardened: Random 128-bit names; the mapping exists only in the encrypted index.
entries.summary: Random 128-bit file names
entries.designDecision: No standard defines archive file naming; random names minimise clear-text metadata.

entries.title: No per-file binding (AAD)
entries.specSays: Silent: nothing binds a file to its name, position or request.
entries.specMinimal: No binding beyond the JWE protected header.
entries.hardened: Protected header carries cxp-path and cxp-req (request digest); both are checked on decryption.
entries.summary: Path and request digest in the authenticated JWE header

standards.role: protected header is the AEAD AAD

entries.title: Archive layout undefined
entries.quote: The format MUST follow the zip archive format as defined in [CXF]
entries.specSays: CXF PS 2026 defines no archive, and the contents of index.jwe and documents/ are unspecified.
entries.specMinimal: Zip with CXP-Export/index.jwe ({header, documents}) and one CXF Item per CXP-Export/documents/<name>.jwe; missing listed documents are skipped, unlisted files ignored.
entries.hardened: The encrypted index lists a SHA-256 per document; missing, unlisted or altered files are rejected.
entries.summary: SHA-256 manifest inside the encrypted index
entries.designDecision: The index/document layout follows the CXP §3.4 illustration; the manifest is a PoC design.

entries.title: No single-use rule or key lifetime
entries.specSays: Silent: no replay rule for a response and no lifetime for the importer key.
entries.specMinimal: The request and its keys remain usable; a response can be imported again.
entries.hardened: The pending request and keyring are discarded after the first successful import (references dropped; JavaScript cannot guarantee erasure).
entries.summary: Importer key discarded after first import

entries.title: Unbounded decompression
entries.quote: The claimed uncompressed size of the DEFLATE compressed data in data.
entries.specSays: Sizes are claims; no limits are set.
entries.specMinimal: No limits; fflate allocates from each entry's declared size.
entries.hardened: Before inflating: at most 10 000 entries, 1 MiB per entry, 64 MiB in total, methods 0/8 only; payload length capped; largeBlob inflated with a 64 KiB bound and checked against uncompressedSize.
entries.summary: Entry/total size caps, payload cap, bounded largeBlob

standards.role: limit decompressed size and file count
declared sizes in local and central headers

entries.designDecision: Numeric limits are PoC choices sized for credential exports.

entries.title: Decrypted key material in memory
entries.specSays: Silent: no guidance on handling decrypted PKCS#8 keys.
entries.specMinimal: No clearing.
entries.hardened: Decrypted file plaintexts, content-encryption keys and the PKCS#8 DER buffer are zeroed after use (best effort: immutable JavaScript strings and GC copies remain).
entries.summary: Best-effort zeroisation of buffers

entries.title: Unauthenticated exporter (base mode)
entries.quote: Base mode of encrypting a public key.
entries.specSays: In base mode the importer cannot authenticate the exporter.
entries.specMinimal: Any well-formed base-mode response is accepted.
entries.hardened: HPKE auth mode with the exporter's static key (sent as hpke.senderKey); the user confirms its fingerprint (GAP-05).
entries.summary: HPKE auth mode with a confirmed exporter key
entries.designDecision: The senderKey member is a PoC extension: CXP has a single key member.

entries.title: Direct-mode transport security
entries.quote: This protocol does not make any assumptions about the channels in which credential data is passed from the source provider to the destination provider.
entries.specSays: No transport security is required.
entries.specMinimal: Plain HTTP on loopback.
entries.hardened: HTTPS with TLS 1.3 minimum and a per-run test CA (server certificate with SAN 127.0.0.1/localhost, serverAuth EKU); the client trusts only that CA and refuses http URLs.
entries.summary: TLS 1.3 with pinned per-run test CA

standards.document: OWASP Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet

entries.title: Importer handling of producer-MUST violations
entries.quote: Identifiers MUST be unique for a given exchanged Account and have a maximum of 64 bytes in length.
entries.specSays: MUSTs bind the producer; the importer's reaction to violations, and b64url padding, are unspecified.
entries.specMinimal: Only structurally malformed input is rejected; padded/non-canonical b64url, any version and any hmac length are accepted.
entries.hardened: Producer-MUST violations rejected: ID length/uniqueness, empty optional arrays, major version 1, PKCS#8 key, canonical unpadded b64url, 32-byte hmac credentials.
entries.summary: Reject producer-MUST violations; canonical base64url

entries.title: No freshness check
entries.quote: The UNIX timestamp in seconds during at which the export document was completed.
entries.specSays: The importer is never told to check it.
entries.specMinimal: Timestamp ignored.
entries.hardened: Reject documents more than 300 s in the future or older than the Export Request (minus 300 s skew).
entries.summary: Timestamp window with 300 s skew
entries.designDecision: The 300 s skew is a PoC choice (a common clock-skew allowance).

entries.title: Two unrelated exporter identities
entries.quote: The name of the exporting app as a relying party identifier.
entries.specSays: Nothing requires the CXF and CXP identities to agree.
entries.specMinimal: No cross-check.
entries.hardened: Header.exporterRpId must equal ExportResponse.exporter (the identity shown when the exporter key is confirmed).
entries.summary: exporterRpId must equal response exporter
entries.designDecision: Consistency check between two self-asserted fields; no standard applies.

entries.title: No required user consent
entries.quote: If an end-user and/or authorizing party approves the request
entries.specSays: Approval is mentioned descriptively only; nothing defines what is shown or binds it to the request.
entries.specMinimal: Supplying the request is the approval.
entries.hardened: A prompt shows importer, request fingerprint, credential types and item count; export proceeds only on approval of that exact request. User verification is simulated (the approval callback stands for it).
entries.summary: Consent prompt bound to the request fingerprint

standards.role: what you see is what you sign

entries.title: Conflicting import
entries.specSays: Silent: nothing covers importing a credential that already exists.
entries.specMinimal: The imported credential replaces the existing one.
entries.hardened: The existing credential is kept and the conflict reported (skipped with reason 'conflict').
entries.summary: Never silently replace an existing credential

standards.document: Saltzer & Schroeder, The Protection of Information in Computer Systems (1975)

entries.title: Indirect-mode file handling
entries.quote: which MUST output the Export Response to the filesystem.
entries.specSays: No guidance on location, permissions or removal.
entries.specMinimal: Default permissions (umask, typically 0644); files left in place.
entries.hardened: Files created with mode 0600; response and request files deleted after a successful import (best effort: storage remanence and backups remain).
entries.summary: 0600 files, deleted after import

entries.title: Clear-text identifiers
entries.quote: Identifiers SHOULD NOT have any personally identifying information contained as they will be shared in clear text during any given [CXP] exchange sessions.
entries.specSays: Identifiers are expected to be visible in clear text.
entries.specMinimal: Item IDs appear as archive file names.
entries.hardened: Realised by GAP-08: random file names, IDs only inside encrypted files.
entries.summary: Via GAP-08 random file names

entries.title: Scope widening by removing credentialTypes
entries.quote: If this member is not present then it is understood that the Importing Provider is requesting all credential types.
entries.specSays: Absence silently means 'all types', so stripping the member widens the export.
entries.specMinimal: Absent = all types.
entries.hardened: An altered request changes its fingerprint (user declines) and its digest in HPKE info (response does not decrypt).
entries.summary: Via GAP-01/05/06 request binding

entries.notClosedReason: Out of protocol scope: CXP excludes source-credential destruction; closing it needs a specification change or provider policy outside CXP.
entries.title: Source copy retained
entries.quote: The destruction of credentials after migration by the credential provider source is out of scope as well.
entries.specSays: Destruction is out of scope.
entries.specMinimal: Source copy retained.
entries.hardened: Same (residual risk, documented).
entries.summary: Not closed (out of scope)
entries.designDecision: Residual risk; recommendation for a future CXP revision.

entries.notClosedReason: Spec-mandated (CXF MUST); a conformant mitigation is impossible, so it requires a specification change.
entries.title: Identical PRF/hmac-secret seeds across importers
entries.quote: If these credentials are exchanged to multiple importing providers who support both values, they MUST all have the same value.
entries.specSays: Every importer receives the same seeds.
entries.specMinimal: As specified.
entries.hardened: As specified (MUST in both profiles).
entries.summary: Not closed (requires spec change)
entries.designDecision: Demonstrated and recommended for a specification change.

entries.notClosedReason: Spec-mandated (CXF MUST: counter zero, never incremented); requires a specification change.
entries.title: Signature counter forced to zero
entries.quote: Importers MUST set a zero value for the imported passkey signature counters and MUST NOT increment them after the fact.
entries.specSays: Disables RP clone detection for migrated passkeys.
entries.specMinimal: As specified.
entries.hardened: As specified (MUST in both profiles).
entries.summary: Not closed (requires spec change)

standards.role: RP signature-counter check that a zero counter disables

entries.notClosedReason: No conformant CXF field carries BE/BS or the AAGUID; requires a CXF change.
entries.title: Backup flags not carried by CXF
entries.specSays: Silent: the Passkey dictionary has no backup-eligibility/state or AAGUID member.
entries.specMinimal: Both authenticators report BE=1, BS=1.
entries.hardened: Same.
entries.summary: Not closed (requires spec change)

standards.role: backup eligibility fixed for the credential lifetime

entries.notClosedReason: Not implemented in the PoC: notifying the owner would need ExportingProvider changes outside the adversary code boundary (the exclusion itself is a CXF MUST and is implemented).
entries.title: Excluded passkeys not reported to the owner
entries.quote: the exporter SHOULD inform the user that such passkeys are excluded from the export.
entries.specSays: Exclusion is a MUST; informing the user is a SHOULD.
entries.specMinimal: Exclusion reported to the calling code (ExportReport.excludedNonZeroCounter) but not to the owner.
entries.hardened: Same.
entries.summary: Not closed (not implemented)
entries.designDecision: No external standard applies: the obligation is the CXF SHOULD itself; recorded as a recommendation (report each excluded credential and the reason to the owner).
